objects.name: Explorer Inputs (Alpaca4d)
objects.desc:
Runs a design study: every combination of the sliders, value lists and panels connected to it, one solution each, for Explorer Record to save and the Alpaca4d Explorer to show.
Press Fly on the component, or set Fly to true, to start. Press it again, or Esc, to stop. Designs already recorded are skipped, so a stopped study goes on where it left off.

objects.name: AssembleModel (Alpaca4d)
objects.desc: Assemble a Model

objects.name: Analysis Settings (Alpaca4d)
objects.desc:
Collects everything OpenSees needs in order to solve - constraint handler, numberer, system of equations, convergence test, solution algorithm, integrator and stepping - into the one object Run Analysis takes.
Every input has a default, so an unconnected component already describes a valid linear static analysis. For a dynamic one set AnalysisType to Transient, and give it a Newmark or Central Difference Integrator, an Analysis Step with Dt, and a Damping.

objects.name: Run Analysis (Alpaca4d)
objects.desc:
Writes the assembled model out as an OpenSees script, solves it, and returns the model with its results attached.
Results are recorded to a recorder.mpco file beside the Grasshopper document and read back by the 08_NumericalOutput components; an MPCO Recorder connected to Assemble Model chooses what the file holds, and what it is called. When a run fails the AlpacaModel output comes out empty - read the log output to find out why.

objects.name: Model View (Alpaca4d)
objects.desc: Visualise the assembled model in the viewport

objects.name: Natural Vibration Analysis (Alpaca4d)
objects.desc:
Solves the eigenvalue problem of the model and returns its modes, eigenvalues, periods and frequencies.
It needs no Analysis Settings - an eigenvalue problem has nothing to converge. Connect the assembled model rather than an analysed one, then feed the solved model to Nodal Displacements to read a mode shape.
The modal report - masses, centre of mass, participation factors and mass ratios - is in the Modal Report menu below the component.

objects.name: Expression

objects.name: Nodal Displacements (Alpaca4d)
objects.desc:
Reads displacement, rotation, velocity and acceleration at every node of an analysed model.
One value per node, in global axes, in assembly order. Velocity and acceleration come from a transient analysis only. After a Natural Vibration Analysis, Step picks the mode and Displacement and Rotation are its shape.
Give NodeTag to read part of a big model.

objects.name: Utilisation (Alpaca4d)
objects.desc:
Checks every beam against the design code of its material and reports how much of each resistance it uses: 1 is exactly at the limit.
Steel, to EN 1993-1-1: cross-section class, then axial force, shear, torsion, bending, and bending with axial force and shear (6.2); flexural buckling about both axes (6.3.1); lateral-torsional buckling (6.3.2), with M_cr worked out on each beam's own moment diagram; and bending with compression as a member (6.3.3, by Annex B). Not yet: torsional buckling and Class 4 sections.
The steel grade comes from the beam's material: make it with Material Library Elastic, or name it after its grade ("S355").
One item per beam, in the order of the Element output. A check that could not be made is empty, never zero, and leaves Max empty too.
Fabrication, the partial factors and the report - and the Type, Class and Governing outputs - are in the Design menu below the component.

Each input is one result, named after the input: rename an input to name its column.

objects.name: Explorer Record (Alpaca4d)
objects.desc:
Saves each design of a study into a folder the Alpaca4d Explorer opens: data.csv with the inputs and results, and a picture and a 3D model of each design.
Set Write to true and press Fly on Explorer Inputs. Designs already saved are not saved again. Right-click to open the folder or the explorer, or to start the study over.

objects.name: Panel
objects.desc: A panel for custom notes and text values
objects.text:
Footbridge design study - the Alpaca4d Explorer example.

Two steel Warren trusses, 2.5 m apart, studied over 4 spans x 3 depths x 3 panel counts x 3 chord sections: 108 designs. Each is analysed under its own weight and a deck load, checked to EN 1993-1-1 and solved for its first natural frequency.

1. Save this definition. The study is recorded next to it, in AlpacaExplorer.
2. Show the bridge in a perspective view in Rhino: each design's picture is taken from the active viewport.
3. Set Write, on Explorer Record, to true.
4. Press Fly under Explorer Inputs. Right-click it > Test fly runs three designs first, to check the pictures.
5. Right-click Explorer Record > Open the Alpaca4d Explorer, and drop the study folder on the page.
